+from .base import get_stats, merge, _count_elements

+def pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop):
+    """
+    Lazy max-heap over pair counts: heap holds (-count, pair) entries, and
+    every pair in stats has an entry with a count >= its current count
+    (increases are pushed by callers, decreases fixed up here). Returns the
+    maximal count and every pair with it (same as max(stats.values())); the
+    candidates' entries are pushed back, keeping the heap invariant.
+    """
+    while True:
+        if not heap:
+            raise ValueError("max() arg is an empty sequence")
+        neg, p = heap[0]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == -neg:
+            break
+        heappop(heap)
+        if c and c < -neg:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p)) # count went down: re-file it (not 0)
+    top = -neg
+    cands = []
+    while heap and heap[0][0] == neg:
+        p = heappop(heap)[1]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == top:
+            if p not in cands:
+                cands.append(p)
+        elif c and c < top:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+    for p in cands:
+        heappush(heap, (neg, p))
+    return top, cands
+
+
+def regex_merge(ids, weights, where, stats, heap, pair, idx):
+    # RegexTokenizer.train merge step: replace pair by idx in the chunks that
+    # hold it (where[pair]), updating pair counts by the difference. New pairs
+    # contain idx, so none is in stats yet and no decrement touches one: they
+    # are counted apart and added at the end. Fast-path merges (one p0 in the
+    # chunk) are subtracted from stats[pair] once at the end.
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    added = {}
+    added_get = added.get
+    fast_total = 0
+    # a merged pair never reappears, so its chunk set can be dropped
+    for k in where.pop(pair, ()):
+        old = ids[k]
+        c = old.count(p0)
+        if c == 1:
+            j = old.index(p0)
+            e = j + 2
+            n_old = len(old)
+            if e > n_old or old[j+1] != p1:
+                continue # stale entry
+            w = weights[k]
+            fast_total += w
+            if j:
+                a = old[j-1]
+                stats[(a, p0)] -= w
+                p = (a, idx)
+                added[p] = added_get(p, 0) + w
+                where[p].append(k)
+            if e < n_old:
+                b = old[e]
+                stats[(p1, b)] -= w
+                p = (idx, b)
+                added[p] = added_get(p, 0) + w
+                where[p].append(k)
+            # splice in place (ids[k] is private to this chunk)
+            old[j] = idx
+            del old[j+1]
+            continue
+        if not c:
+            continue # stale entry
+        new = merge(old, pair, idx)
+        n_old = len(old)
+        m = n_old - len(new) # number of merged occurrences
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        ids[k] = new
+        w = weights[k]
+        stats[pair] -= w * m
+        # new[q] == idx marks exactly the merged occurrences
+        index = new.index
+        q = -1
+        for c in range(m):
+            q = index(idx, q + 1)
+            j = q + c # position of this occurrence in old
+            if q:
+                a = new[q-1]
+                if a != idx: # else counted by the adjacent previous one
+                    stats[(a, p0)] -= w
+                    p = (a, idx)
+                    added[p] = added_get(p, 0) + w
+                    where[p].append(k)
+            if j + 2 < n_old:
+                stats[(p1, old[j+2])] -= w
+                p = (idx, new[q+1])
+                added[p] = added_get(p, 0) + w
+                where[p].append(k)
+    stats[pair] -= fast_total
+    stats.update(added)
+    for p, c in added.items():
+        heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+

journal.text:
I moved the per-merge chunk update out of RegexTokenizer.train in minbpe/regex.py and into minbpe/_train.py as regex_merge, which train now calls once per merge. Encoding imports minbpe.regex, and that import was compiling the whole merge step and pulling in heapq and defaultdict even though encoding never trains. Along the way I made and reverted some edits to base.py and a _slow.py file.

My sandbox evaluation was accepted with identical outputs. encode_ir went from 387145280 to 382877245, ratio 0.9890. train_ir went from 313804564 to 314185357, ratio 1.0012, which is within guard limits. The diff is 162 lines across 2 files. It is submitted and queued for replay, so there is no verdict yet.

I believe import-time cost is a real share of encode_ir here, and that keeping train-only code out of modules on the encode path pays off. The extra call per merge costs train a little.

Next I would look for other train-only imports or definitions still loaded on the encode path in base.py and regex.py. I would also check whether inlining reduces the train_ir regression.
